newsitem.title: GERMANY: DTB Bund futures seen retreating after new high.
newsitem.headline: DTB Bund futures seen retreating after new high.

text.p: German Bund futures enjoyed a buoyant session on Wednesday but failed to deliver a convincing rally after spiking to a fresh high in early business.
"The market has a positive tone to it and we have made some new highs today, but it is starting to look a little bit stretched," said Martin Ballans, futures strategist at Cooperative Bank in London.

Analysts said that the absence of follow-through buying after the September future reached a new contract high at 102.16 earlier in the session suggested that prices would settle back in the near-term, looking to consolidate.
By 1420 GMT, the September DTB Bund contract was 13 basis points higher on the day at 102.03 having traded in a range of 101.84 to 102.16 during the session.
Based on technicals, September DTB Bunds were also set for a phase of consolidation at firm levels, but keeping upside targets -- now at 102.32 to 102.35 -- in mind.
Continuation charts show daily highs were plotted at 102.32 and 102.35 in mid-May.
In the cash market, traders said the 30-year auction past smoothly but, said some nervousness remained with memories of the last German 30-year bond still in the market.
"People are still a bit wary of Germany 30-years," said Ballans. "The Bundesbank seems to have a knack of picking the top of the market."

The main events for the remainder of the week would come from the U.S., analysts said. The Federal Reserve's FOMC policy-setting meeting is expected to reach a decision on interst rates later this session, but most market watchers predict that rates will remain on hold.
Beyond that, the U.S. monthly job report is due on Thursday -- a day earlier than usual because of the July 4 Independence Day holiday.

Economists polled by Reuters are forecasting that 336,000 jobs will have been added to the U.S. non-fram payroll in June, compared with 332,000 in May. The unemployment rate is expected to remain steady at 4.8 percent.

For Bunds, a move by the Fed to hold interest rates steady and a payroll figure in line with forecasts could have a positive impact on prices in the very short term, but traders said the market is likely to resume its rather wary range-trading activity before the week is out.
